title: California Gray Wolf Monitoring
description: California gray wolf pack territory polygons and CDFW collar-derived position cells. IMPORTANT — THESE ARE CELLS, NOT POINTS: CDFW does not publish GPS fixes. Collar locations are aggregated to hexagonal cells (H3 resolution 6, ~37 km² — about 6 km flat-to-flat and 7.7 km corner-to-corner) sized to match average daily wolf movement, and the cell is the finest location this dataset contains. Any point rendered from it (a centroid, a track vertex, an animated dot) is a label for a cell, not a location, and carries no sub-cell precision. NO PATH IS KNOWN BETWEEN CELLS: positions arrive as a sequence of ~2-hourly snapshots, so consecutive cells say where a wolf was reported, never the route between them. Do not read line or animation geometry drawn through cell centroids as a travelled path, a distance travelled, or a speed. Territory polygons are convex-hull approximations digitized from the official CDFW Approximate Area of Gray Wolf Activity map (February 2025) for six confirmed packs: Whaleback, Harvey, Ice Cave, Lassen, Diamond/Beyem Seyo, and Yowlumni. Boundary polygons are approximate (±5–10 km) and intended for visualization, not legal or management purposes. Snapshots are collected hourly from the CDFW Wolf Location Map; only new data (detected by Last-Modified header) is archived. IMPORTANT SAMPLING LIMITATIONS: (1) Only a subset of wolves in a subset of packs are GPS-collared; packs with higher livestock-conflict potential are prioritized for collaring, so coverage is biased, not representative, and neither wolves nor packs can be counted from it. (2) The `pack` field is an individual wolf identifier, not a pack; the associated pack is the separate `pack_origin` field, and CDFW renames individuals from time to time. (3) Collars typically collect 4 fixes/day (3 dusk-to-dawn, 1 midday); frequency may increase seasonally for research. (4) Transmission can be delayed by weather or dense forest cover. (5) During denning/rendezvous season (April–August), CDFW suppresses cells near den and rendezvous sites to protect sensitive locations; absence of active cells in a known territory does not mean the pack is absent. (6) If a collar stops reporting, the map continues to show its last known cell — compare `most_recent_adj` (CDFW's last-fix date) against the snapshot time before treating a cell as current. (7) When multiple collars occupy the same cell, only one cell is shown. This data was designed for livestock-conflict mitigation, not ecological monitoring.

territories.title: Wolf pack territory polygons (February 2025)
territories.description: Six pack territory polygons digitized from the CDFW Approximate Area of Gray Wolf Activity map (Feb 2025): Whaleback, Harvey, Ice Cave, Lassen, Diamond/Beyem Seyo, Yowlumni. Convex-hull approximations, ~5–10 km accuracy: these are approximate areas of activity, not territory boundaries, home ranges, or administrative limits. Static reference layer; areas and overlaps computed from them are approximate, and differences between packs are not measured differences.

bins-latest.title: Latest reported wolf cells (~6 km hexes, visualization)
bins-latest.description: Most recent CDFW snapshot of reported wolf positions as H3 resolution-6 hexagonal polygons (~37 km², ~6 km flat-to-flat) in GeoJSON. Used by the map's latest-cells layer. Each feature is a cell a collar reported from, carrying the individual wolf id (`pack`), its pack (`pack_origin`), and CDFW's last-fix date (`most_recent_adj`). For SQL queries use trail-hex with `WHERE last_seen_ts = (SELECT MAX(last_seen_ts) FROM trail-hex)` instead — it has H3 cells for fast joins.

tracks.title: Wolf cell-to-cell sequences (map playback, visualization)
tracks.description: Per-wolf LineStrings through the centroids of consecutively reported hexbin cells over the past 30 days, used by the map's playback layer. THE LINE GEOMETRY IS NOT AN OBSERVED PATH — it connects cell centroids in reporting order and no part of it between two vertices was observed. Each vertex carries the window its cell was reported over: `timestamps` (first reported) and `end_timestamps` (last reported) are arrays parallel to the coordinates, which lets the map show each cell only while it was actually being reported instead of sliding a dot between them. `pack` is the individual wolf, `pack_origin` its pack. Visualization only — for SQL movement queries, use trail-hex.

snapshots.title: Raw CDFW snapshot archive
snapshots.description: Time-stamped archive of every distinct CDFW wolf-bins GeoJSON observed by the hourly fetcher. Filename encodes the upstream Last-Modified timestamp (UTC). Provenance / replay use only — for analytical queries use trail-hex.

trail-hex.title: Wolf movement trail (H3 res-8 tiled, h0-partitioned, 30-day rolling)
trail-hex.description: PRIMARY ANALYTICAL ASSET. Past 30 days of reported wolf positions, polyfilled to H3 resolution 8 cells. One row per (wolf, reported cell, reporting window, h8): CDFW republishes a wolf's cell in every snapshot until it moves, so consecutive republications of the same cell collapse into a single row spanning `snapshot_ts` (first reported) to `last_seen_ts` (last reported); a wolf missing from intervening snapshots breaks the window, so gaps in reporting survive into the data. Current positions are `WHERE last_seen_ts = (SELECT MAX(last_seen_ts) FROM trail)` — keying off MAX(snapshot_ts) instead drops every wolf that hasn't changed cells lately. Note the source cell is CDFW's H3 resolution-6 hexbin (~37 km²); the resolution-8 cells here are a tiling of it for joining, not a finer measurement, so COUNT(*) counts index cells — count DISTINCT _cng_fid for observations. Hive-partitioned by h0 — California fits in a single h0 cell, but the column is exposed so dynamic partition pruning works when joining against globally-partitioned catalog datasets. Hash-join on h8 with any other catalog hex asset; prune time windows on snapshot_ts / last_seen_ts (UTC TIMESTAMP). Rebuilt hourly by overwriting the file in place.

table:columns.name: _cng_fid
table:columns.description: Synthetic source-feature id (one per CDFW hex polygon at a given snapshot)

table:columns.name: pack
table:columns.description: Individual collared wolf identifier (e.g. 'CA091 (previously Yowlumni Disperser)') — not a pack, and renamed upstream from time to time

table:columns.name: pack_origin
table:columns.description: Pack the collared wolf is associated with (e.g. 'Whaleback', 'Harvey', 'Beyem Seyo') — the stable label for grouping and styling

table:columns.name: most_recent_adj
table:columns.description: CDFW last-fix date (MM/DD/YYYY) — compare against the snapshot time to tell a current cell from a non-reporting collar's last known cell

table:columns.name: snapshot_ts
table:columns.description: UTC timestamp of the snapshot that first reported this wolf in this cell

table:columns.name: last_seen_ts
table:columns.description: UTC timestamp of the last consecutive snapshot still reporting this wolf in this cell (equal to snapshot_ts for a single-snapshot report)

table:columns.name: h8
table:columns.description: H3 cell ID at resolution 8 — one of several tiling CDFW's resolution-6 source hexbin, for joining (not a finer position)

table:columns.name: h0
table:columns.description: H3 cell ID at resolution 0 (partition key — enables DPP against global hex datasets)
